sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Ronnenberg, a town on the south-western edge of Hannover with the districts Weetzen and Empelde, regulates parking lightly, and what we found are old council records and not a current rulebook. We found no parking-fee, resident-parking or parking-space statute. A council meeting in January 2020 reported that no signs had yet been put up for a time-limited parking-disc rule on a section of Bröhnstraße in Weetzen, and the page does not show whether they were installed later [1]. In June 2021 residents told the council that many cars park without a disc on Nenndorfer Straße and its side streets, and the mayor said the city was checking more often there [2]. Enforcement is carried out by six marginally employed staff giving about 50 hours a week, with fines processed by the Region Hannover, and its aim is traffic education and not maximum revenue, according to a reply of September 2025 [3]. The same reply explains that under the state building code parking spaces no longer have to be provided for dwellings if the application was submitted after 30 June 2024 [4]. At an expert meeting for the town development concept in 2015, the administration said building permits normally required two parking spaces per dwelling and that garages are often used as storerooms, so cars end up in the street [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The development is about the park-and-ride sites and bus links. In its comments on the Region's transport development plan VEP 2035+ of June 2022, the city said an extension of the park-and-ride lots at Weetzen and Linderte/Holtensen should be examined, noting that the Region's utilisation studies gave low priority to more park-and-ride in the town, and asked for roofed, lockable bike parking and charging at the sites [10]. The Region's local transport plan of 2020 rated the Weetzen P+R as category 1, high priority, and said use was currently free but fees might make sense for some users [8]. The 70-space P+R at Hermann-Ehlers-Allee, on the Hannover side of the border with Empelde, opened on 20 March 2024 with a sensor in every space, and the 80-space P+R at the Empelde terminus of Stadtbahn line 9 was mostly completely occupied in 2024 [12][13]. The Region decided in November 2024 to extend the sprintH line 500 to Weetzen station as a three-year trial, running every 10 minutes on weekdays, with an average of 770 passengers boarding per weekday at the stop on three lines together in the third quarter of 2025 [14]. On charging, the city reports 45 public charge points at 17 sites, with 22 kW points at the Empelde, Ronnenberg and Weetzen P+R sites, and EnBW has run four fast chargers at the Chemnitzer Straße retail centre since February 2024 [16][17]. Stadtmobil has offered three cars in Empelde since April 2025, one of them at the P+R [15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Deutsche Bahn lists the Weetzen P+R at An den Kleingärten with 197 spaces, open round the clock, without a tariff, while the Region put it at 196 spaces in 2021, when it counted Weetzen among five pilot sites whose occupancy is recorded digitally [6][9]. The city of Hannover's page says all park-and-ride sites in the GVH area are free to use [7].

Our data cover the P+R Weetzen, with 196 spaces, for about 27 days since late September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 33% on weekdays and 18% at weekends, with a peak of 68% in the morning of a Tuesday, which fits a commuter car park. The Empelde and Ronnenberg station car parks are not in our data.
